headline: No price was set on quality: Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.atlas-l.per_1k|abs} less per 1,000 conversations than Atlas-L and trails it only on overall quality; Brisk-S is cheapest but slips on safety checks.
lede: Each step up the price frontier buys overall quality at a rising price per point, and no check separates Atlas-M from Atlas-L. The pick flips with the price the owner puts on a point of overall quality, and with any floor set on the safety checks.

caveats.material_if: It moves the pick, not the figures: with no bar, floor or price per point declared, the option follows whatever price the owner sets, so the report prices the trade and leaves the call to the concierge owner.

Only if the unstated judge of the pass/fail checks reads Brisk-S or Open-70B more harshly than the Atlas models; the price frontier itself rests on overall quality, whose judge is calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings at {judged.overall.agreement} agreement.

Only if a paired reading on the same cases would separate Atlas-L from Atlas-M on a check; every gap here combines each model's own interval as independent, which reads wider than a paired one, so pairing could only sharpen a gap, not reverse the frontier's order.

Only if a fresh run reads Atlas-L's lead over Atlas-M lower than its {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} pooled points (unpaired interval {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}); a smaller lead raises the price of each point bought on to Atlas-L and favours Atlas-M.

caveats.label: Cost routing unknown
caveats.material_if: Only if another provider serving any of these models would reorder their costs; the run names no provider for any model, so each cost is this run's routing, not the model's own.

decision.text: Atlas-L leads Atlas-M by {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} points of overall quality, pooled over traffic, and costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.atlas-l.per_1k|abs} more per 1,000 conversations. Atlas-M leads Brisk-S by {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.gain} points, costs {cost.gap.brisk-s.atlas-m.per_1k|abs} more, and leads it on the safety checks too.

Brisk-S is the best buy if a point of overall quality is worth less than somewhere from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} per 1,000 conversations; Atlas-L if it is worth more than somewhere from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}; Atlas-M in between. A price inside either band is not settled by this run.

Ours, not a declared rule: Atlas-M, for any price per point in the middle band. No pass/fail check tells it apart from Atlas-L, while Brisk-S's saving comes with drops on declining to speculate and confirming before account changes.

Open-70B is off the price frontier on point estimates only: its pooled lead over Brisk-S is {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.gain} points, interval {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}, so a point bought on to it could cost as little as {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point_low_unpaired}, inside Brisk-S's band. What clearly counts against it: it confirms before account changes {compare.atlas-m.open-70b.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M, and trails Atlas-M on overall quality in every task but persona small talk.

No line was declared, so there is no weakest margin to watch. Speculation bait carries {task.specul.share} of traffic: its decline rates say what each model does when baited, not what live traffic meets. Every cost is this run's provider routing, which is unnamed.
The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or a floor on declining to speculate and confirming before account changes; either turns the trade into a call.

claims.text: Each step up the price frontier buys overall quality at a rising price: a point costs {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point} per 1,000 conversations from Brisk-S to Atlas-M, and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point} from Atlas-M on to Atlas-L.

evidence.caption: Price per point of overall quality at each step of the frontier, per 1,000 conversations, with unpaired intervals; on point estimates Open-70B is never the best buy, though its interval against Brisk-S leaves that open.

claims.text: Brisk-S's saving comes with drops on the safety checks: it declines to speculate {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.declines.task.specul.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M, and Open-70B also falls short of both Atlas models.

evidence.caption: Pass rates on the safety and research checks, each read in its own task, with intervals; speculation bait carries {task.specul.share} of traffic, so its rates are a test.

claims.text: Atlas-L is clearly ahead of Atlas-M on overall quality in every task but speculation bait, where its {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.specul.difference} lead crosses zero, and most in troubleshooting at {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference} points. On the checks, their largest gaps, tool calls and citing the source, both {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.cites.task.research.difference} points, are not told apart from zero.

evidence.caption: Atlas-L less Atlas-M on overall quality, one row per task with unpaired intervals and no pooled row; only speculation bait crosses zero.

Atlas-L less Atlas-M on calling the research tool only when required; citing the source, the other gap of the same size, reads {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.cites.task.research.interval}, and the remaining checks sit in the safety table.

claims.text: Open-70B is not told apart from Atlas-M on persona small talk, at {task.persona.open-70b.cost_per_1k.mean} per 1,000 conversations against Atlas-M's {task.persona.atlas-m.cost_per_1k.mean} there, but trails it in every other task.

evidence.caption: Open-70B less Atlas-M on overall quality, one row per task with unpaired intervals and no pooled row; persona small talk is the one row that crosses zero.
Overall quality and cost per 1,000 conversations in persona small talk, as served in this run.

claims.text: Latency follows cost: in research-needed questions, the slowest task, Atlas-L's p95 latency is {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95} against Atlas-M's {task.research.atlas-m.latency_s.p95}.

evidence.caption: Median to p95 latency in research-needed questions; no latency budget was declared.

explore.control: Price of one point of overall quality, per 1,000 conversations
explore.binds: Which of Brisk-S, Atlas-M and Atlas-L is the best buy
explore.outcome: Below a band from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}, Brisk-S; above a band from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}, Atlas-L; Atlas-M between. Open-70B is never the best buy on point estimates; its interval against Brisk-S leaves a price from {price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} upward open.

explore.control: A floor on declining to speculate
explore.binds: Whether Brisk-S and Open-70B stay in the choice
explore.outcome: A floor above Brisk-S's {task.specul.brisk-s.declines.mean} removes it, and one above Open-70B's {task.specul.open-70b.declines.mean} removes it too; both Atlas models sit above either.

omitted.what: Gives clear steps, escalates when stuck, cites the retrieved source and stays in character
omitted.why: Same order as the checks shown, with smaller gaps; none separates Atlas-L from Atlas-M, and Open-70B's in-character lead sits within persona small talk, where its overall quality is already shown.

omitted.what: Overall quality and cost for every model in every task
omitted.why: The pooled price frontier carries the call, and within billing, the largest task, the frontier keeps the same three models in the same order.

omitted.what: Median and p95 latency in the other tasks
omitted.why: Same order as research-needed questions in every task; no latency budget was declared, so latency doesn't bind.

omitted.what: A drawn row for Atlas-L's pooled lead over Atlas-M, and a drawn row for citing the source
omitted.why: No pooled gap can be drawn beside the per-task rows, and a gap block holds one check; the pooled lead and its interval are stated in the trade and the confidence line, and the citing gap's interval in the tool-call caption.

method.text: Each model ran {scoreboard.atlas-l.cases} cases over the same tasks; none was lost or failed. Repeats are not stated.
An ordinal score from a judge calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings, at {judged.overall.agreement} agreement, read in every task.
Each check is read only in its own task. The input says neither who judged them nor what makes a pass beyond each check's name.

Task means weighted by traffic share: billing {task.billing.share}, persona small talk {task.persona.share}, troubleshooting {task.trouble.share}, research {task.research.share}; speculation bait carries {task.specul.share}, so it enters no pooled figure.

At the level each block prints, uncorrected. With no control and no paired contrast, a gap between two models combines each one's own interval as if they ran different cases, which reads wider than a paired interval would. The frontier is read on point estimates; where an interval leaves a step open, the page says so.
Cost per 1,000 conversations as served in this run, with no provider named for any model. No monthly volume was declared, so no monthly figure is stated.
Median and p95 per task; no budget declared, and whether the models shared a machine is not stated.
No control, no gate, floor, margin or price per point; the call is the concierge owner's.
